  * A link to a nested entry opens that entry, rather than stopping at the first segment of its path and opening the wrong one.\[^370] See [entry shorthand links](/en/docs/ui/content-editor#opening-specific-entries).
  * A deep tree keeps working, whatever `nested.depth` is set to: the file list comes from a single recursive request, so the backend never gives up on the collection.\[^371]

### Better Content Editing

* Required fields, not optional fields, are marked for efficient data entry.
* Users can revert changes to all fields or a specific field. They can also restore the default values or clear the values of a field, of the fields in a locale, or of the whole entry, which comes in handy to start over. The options that change many fields at once ask for confirmation first. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/1022))
* If changes are reverted and there are no unsaved changes, the Save button is disabled as expected.\[^118]
* The new `readonly` field option makes the field read-only. This is useful when a `default` value is provided and the field should not be editable by users.\[^223] The option defaults to `false` except for the UUID widget, where it defaults to `true`.
* An entry can be validated manually while editing using the Validation sidebar panel.
* Fields with validation errors are automatically expanded if they are part of nested, collapsed objects.\[^40]
* A full regular expression, including flags, can be used for the widget `pattern` option.\[^82] For example, if you want to allow 280 characters or less in a multiline text field, you could write `/^.{0,280}$/s` (but you can now use the `maxlength` option instead.)
* The new [`unique` field option](/en/docs/fields#unique) makes sure a value isn’t used in the same field of any other entry in the collection, like a `UNIQUE` constraint in a relational database. It works with the String, Text, Number, Color, DateTime, Markdown and RichText fields, as well as the File, Image, Relation and Select fields taking a single value.\[^403]
* A long validation error message is displayed in full, without being hidden behind the field label.\[^59]
* Any links to other entries will work as expected, with the Content Editor being updated for the other.\[^100]
* In the Boolean and Select widgets, users don’t have to update a value twice to re-enable the Save button after saving an entry.\[^139]
* `data` can be used as a field name without causing an error when saving the entry.\[^180]
* The entry content is validated before loading to prevent crashes caused by invalid data, such as values of the wrong type.\[^347]
* Changes made by other people are noticed. Netlify/Decap CMS writes an entry from the copy loaded when the site data was fetched, so a change a colleague pushed in the meantime is overwritten without a word. Sveltia CMS checks the repository as an entry is opened, every minute while the tab is shown, and again before every save, and only what has changed is fetched:
  * An entry is opened as it is on the branch, not as it was when the site data was loaded, and the entry and asset lists follow the repository as commits land.
  * If someone changes the entry that is open, a notice says who and when and offers to reload it. Work in progress is left alone either way.
  * If the user saves anyway, Sveltia CMS asks first, so the other change is never overwritten by accident. See [Conflict Resolution](/en/docs/ui/content-editor#conflict-resolution).
  * On GitHub, the branch head the loaded data reflects is passed to the commit API as the expected head, so a commit against a branch that has moved is refused by GitHub itself. Netlify/Decap CMS looks the head up right before committing, which defeats the check, and the rare case where two people save at the same moment fails with an unexplained `Update is not a fast forward` error.\[^376] Sveltia CMS explains what happened and picks the other change up before the next attempt.

### Better Content Preview

* The Preview Pane comes with a minimal default style.\[^168] It looks nice without a custom preview style or template.
* For better performance, the Preview Pane doesn’t use an `<iframe>` unless a custom preview stylesheet is registered.\[^179]
* The Preview Pane displays all fields, including each label, making it easier to see which fields are populated.
* Entering a long value into a field will not cause the field label to disappear.\[^254]
* Clicking a field in the Preview Pane focuses the corresponding field in the Edit Pane.\[^41] It automatically expands when collapsed.
  * This is equivalent to the (misleading) visual editing feature introduced in [Decap CMS 3.6.0](https://github.com/decaporg/decap-cms/releases/tag/decap-cms%403.6.0), but our click-to-highlight feature is enabled by default; you don’t need to opt in with the `editor.visualEditing` collection option. We don’t plan to support this option because it’s confusing, unnecessary and undocumented. (Plus, why camel case?)
* The Preview Pane doesn’t cause a scrolling issue.\[^136]
* The Preview Pane doesn’t crash with a Minified React error.\[^186]\[^334]\[^335]
* Provides better scroll synchronization between the panes when editing or previewing an entry.\[^92]
* Developers can hide the preview of a specific field using a new field option: `preview: false`.\[^126]
* [See below](#better-widgets) for widget-specific enhancements, including support for variable types\[^42] and YouTube videos.

### Better Data Output

* Keys in generated JSON/TOML/YAML content are always sorted by the order of configured fields, making Git commits clean and consistent.\[^86]
* Netlify/Decap CMS often, but not always, omits optional and empty fields from the output.\[^154] Sveltia CMS aims at complete and consistent data output — it always saves proper values, such as an empty string, an empty array or `null`, instead of nothing (`undefined`), regardless of the `required` field option.\[^45]\[^46]\[^44]\[^157]
  * In other words, in Sveltia CMS, `required: false` makes data input optional, but doesn’t make data output optional.
  * To omit empty optional fields from data output, use `omit_empty_optional_fields: true` in the [data output options](/en/docs/data-output#controlling-data-output). This is useful if you have data type validations that expect `undefined`.\[^156]
* JSON/TOML/YAML data is saved with a new line at the end of the file to prevent unnecessary changes being made to the file.\[^11]
* Leading/trailing whitespaces in text-type field values are automatically removed when an entry is saved.\[^37] No option is required to trim the values.\[^275] Code field values are kept as they are, and multiline text values keep their leading whitespace.
* Strings that a YAML 1.1 parser would read as a boolean or a number, such as `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` and `1:20`, are quoted in YAML output, so tools still using YAML 1.1, such as Jekyll, read them as strings.
* YAML string folding (maximum line width) is disabled, mainly for framework compatibility.\[^119]
* A standard time is formatted as `HH:mm:ss` instead of `HH:mm` for framework compatibility, including Hugo.
* DateTime field values in ISO 8601 format are stored in native date/time format instead of quoted strings when the data output is TOML.\[^147]
* Provides JSON/YAML format options as part of the [data output options](/en/docs/data-output#controlling-data-output), including indentation and quotes.\[^155]\[^9]
* It’s impossible to inject front matter through the `body` field.\[^268]

### Better Widgets

Sveltia CMS supports all the [built-in widgets](/en/docs/fields#field-types) available in Netlify/Decap CMS. We have improved these widgets significantly while adding some new ones.

* [Boolean](/en/docs/fields/boolean)
  * A required Boolean field with no default value is saved as `false` by default, without raising a confusing validation error.\[^45]
  * An optional Boolean field with no default value is also saved as `false` by default, rather than nothing.\[^46]
* [Code](/en/docs/fields/code)
  * More than 240 languages are available, thanks to [Shiki](https://shiki.style/)’s extensive language support.
  * The language switcher always appears in the user interface, so it’s easy to spot and change the selected language.
  * Dynamic loading of language modes work as expected.\[^198]
  * A Code field under a List field work as expected, saving both code and language.\[^181]
  * A wrong initial value will not cause a crash with a `TypeError`.\[^257]
* [Color](/en/docs/fields/color)
  * The widget doesn’t cause scrolling issues.\[^128]
  * The preview shows both the RGB(A) hex value and the `rgb()` function notation.
* [DateTime](/en/docs/fields/datetime)
  * Powerful new options for better date/time input control:
    * The new `type` option allows selecting between `datetime-local` (default), `date`, and `time` inputs more intuitively, replacing the confusing `date_format: false` / `time_format: false` workarounds from Netlify/Decap CMS.
    * The new `min` and `max` options allow restricting the selectable date/time range, mapping directly to the HTML `min` and `max` attributes.
    * The new `step` option controls the increment of the date/time input, mapping directly to the HTML `step` attribute. For `datetime-local` and `time`, the value is in seconds (e.g. `900` for 15-minute steps); for `date`, the value is in days (e.g. `7` for weekly steps).
    * The new `input_timezone` and `output_utc` options provide better control over timezones for date/time input and output than the legacy `picker_utc` option.
    * The new `auto_now` option sets the value to the current date/time when an entry is saved, making it easy to keep track of when an entry was created and last modified.\[^380]
    * The new `localize_format` option writes month names and other locale-dependent parts of a custom format in a language other than English, either in a given locale or in each content locale.\[^419]
  * A DateTime field doesn’t trigger a change in the content draft status when a user has just started editing a new entry.\[^90]
  * User’s local time is not saved in UTC unless the `picker_utc` option is `true`.\[^150]
  * The widget doesn’t throw a `RangeError` for formatting days of the month.\[^250]\[^319]
  * The year will not unexpectedly change to `190x` when the value is entered manually.\[^346]
* [Hidden](/en/docs/fields/hidden)
  * The `default` value supports the following template tags:
    * `{{locale}}`: The current locale code.\[^101]
    * `{{datetime}}`: The current date/time in [ISO 8601 format](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date#date_time_string_format).\[^102]
    * `{{uuid}}`, `{{uuid_short}}` and `{{uuid_shorter}}`: A random UUID or its shorter version, just like the [slug template tags](/en/docs/collections/entries/slugs#slug-template-tags).\[^12]
    * `{{author-email}}`, `{{author-login}}` and `{{author-name}}`: The signed-in user’s email, login name and display name, respectively.\[^305]
  * The `default` value is saved when you create a file collection item, not just a folder collection item.\[^78]
* [List](/en/docs/fields/list)
  * It’s possible to [edit data files with a top-level list](/en/docs/fields/list#top-level-list) using the new `root` option.\[^148]
  * A list can be [stored as a map keyed by a subfield](/en/docs/fields/list#keyed-list) using the new `map_key_field` option, so a file format where each item has a unique key, like a Hayagriva bibliography, can be edited with a List field. The keys are validated to be unique, and the map works at the top level of a TOML file too. A key can be typed, or picked with a Relation or Select field, e.g. to store settings for each page keyed by its slug. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/1077), [#1082](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/1082))
  * The `min` and `max` options can be used separately. You don’t need to specify both to use either option.\[^145]
  * The Add Item button appears at the bottom of the list when the `add_to_top` option is not `true`, so you don’t have to scroll up each time to add new items.
  * A list item comes with a menu that allows users to duplicate the item, insert a new item above/below it, or remove it.\[^187]
  * Users can expand or collapse the entire list, while the Expand All and Collapse All buttons allow users to expand or collapse all items in the list at once.\[^164]
  * A required List field with no subfield or value is marked as invalid.\[^43] No need to set the `min` and `max` options for the `required` option to work.
  * An optional List field with no subfield or value is saved as an empty array, rather than nothing.\[^44]
  * An optional List field won’t populate an item by default when the subfield has the `default` value.\[^162]
  * A simple List field with no subfields is displayed as a row per item, which includes a drag handler and single-line text input.\[^219] Users can use spaces\[^50] and commas\[^220] for list items. A comma is no longer treated as a list delimiter.
  * Users can preview variable types without having to register a preview template.\[^42]
  * It’s possible to omit `fields` in a variable type object.\[^163] In that case, only the `typeKey` (default: `type`) is saved in the output.
  * Unknown variable types can be removed and reordered in the list, just like known types.\[^362]
  * A collapsed List field will not display a programmatic summary like `List [ Map { "key": "value" } ]` if the `summary` option is not set.\[^183]
  * The `allow_remove` and `allow_reorder` options can be used to prevent users from removing items and reordering them, respectively.\[^272]
  * The `allow_duplicate` option can be used to prevent users from duplicating items.
  * In a list with 3 or more items, an item can be moved to the top, to the bottom or to a given position from a menu, without dragging it through a long list. This also works for the files in a multiple File/Image field and the pairs in a KeyValue field.
  * A list item can be copied and pasted into any list that takes it, in another entry, collection or browser tab. The values are matched to the subfields by name, and file paths are updated for the target entry, copying a file stored next to the source entry if needed. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/609))
  * A List field limited to one item with `max: 1` is shown like an Object field, without the item count and the list controls, and a required one comes with its item, so there’s no need to add it first. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/1021))
* [Map](/en/docs/fields/map)
  * The `center` and `zoom` options are available to set the initial map view.
  * A search bar enables users to quickly locate a specific place on the map.\[^252]
  * With the [Geolocation API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Geolocation_API), users can get their current location with one click.
  * The value can be cleared by clicking the Clear button.
  * The map’s zoom level is adjusted more intuitively using pinch gestures.
  * The map looks good in dark mode.
* [Markdown](/en/docs/fields/markdown)
  * The rich text editor is built with the well-maintained [Lexical framework](https://lexical.dev/), which solves various issues with a [Slate](https://github.com/ianstormtaylor/slate)-based editor in Netlify/Decap CMS,\[^235] including fatal application crashes,\[^71]\[^72]\[^73]\[^111]\[^374]\[^400] lost formatting when pasting,\[^124]\[^311] an extra line break when pasting,\[^169] extra HTML comments when pasting,\[^229] backslash injections,\[^53] dropdown visibility,\[^70] and text input difficulties with IME.\[^54]
  * For [better security](#better-security), the `sanitize_preview` option defaults to `true` since [Sveltia CMS 0.105.0](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/releases/tag/v0.105.0).
  * The default editor mode can be set by changing the order of the `modes` option.\[^58] If you want to use the plain text editor by default, add `modes: [raw, rich_text]` to the field configuration.
  * The raw Markdown editor comes with syntax highlighting.\[^378]
  * The toolbar buttons also work in the raw Markdown editor, inserting Markdown into the text. Editor components can be inserted as well.\[^379]
  * A Markdown field plays well with a variable type List field.\[^202]
  * The bullet list marker is a hyphen (`-`) rather than an asterisk (`*`), which is the comment form’s default behavior on GitHub and GitLab.\[^296]
  * A combination of bold and italic doesn’t create a confusing 3-asterisk markup.\[^160] In our editor, bold is 2 asterisks and italic is an underscore.
  * Links are edited in a floating link editor.\[^393]
  * When deleting a linked text, the link is removed cleanly without leaving behind any unwanted characters.\[^298]
  * Bare URLs are rendered as clickable links in the preview.\[^312]
  * An editor component can be removed with a single click on the Remove button.\[^310]
  * The built-in `image` component can be inserted with a single click.
  * The built-in `image` component allows users to add, edit or remove a link on an image.\[^171] To disable this feature, add `linked_images: false` to the Markdown field options.
  * It’s possible to paste/drop local/remote images into the rich text editor to insert them as expected. Note: Pasting multiple images is [not supported in Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=864052). In Netlify/Decap CMS, pasting an image may cause the application to crash.\[^284]
  * Inline images are supported.\[^326]
  * The built-in `code-block` component is implemented just like a blockquote. Users can simply convert a normal paragraph into a code block instead of adding a component.
  * The new built-in [`table` component](/en/docs/fields/richtext#tables) allows users to insert a table and edit its rows and columns with a menu, just like the [Lexical Playground](https://playground.lexical.dev/). The Tab key moves between the cells. Add `table` to the `editor_components` option to enable it.\[^256]
  * The new built-in [`hr` component](/en/docs/fields/richtext#editor-components) allows users to insert a horizontal rule with a toolbar button. Add `hr` to the `editor_components` option to enable it.\[^405]
  * Nested editor components can be controlled with the new `allow_nested_components` option.
  * Code in a code block in the editor can be copied as expected.\[^165]
  * Language-annotated code block doesn’t trigger unsaved changes.\[^189]
  * Soft line breaks are [rendered as hard line breaks](/en/docs/how-tos#rendering-soft-line-breaks-as-hard-line-breaks-in-markdown) in the Preview Pane.
  * Uploaded images will not disappear while editing an entry.\[^278]\[^294]
  * The Preview pane is updated instantly while editing.\[^345]
  * It’s possible to [define option defaults](/en/docs/fields/richtext#global-field-defaults) for all Markdown/RichText fields globally.
  * Markdown shortcuts, such as `#` for headings, `-` for bullet lists, and `1.` for numbered lists, are supported in the rich text editor.
* [Number](/en/docs/fields/number)
  * If the `value_type` option is `int` (default) or `float`, the `required` option is `false`, and the value is not entered, the field will be saved as `null` instead of an empty string.\[^157]
  * The `value_type` option accepts `int/string` and `float/string` to save the number as a string instead of a number.
  * The up and down buttons and arrow keys can be turned off with [`step: -1`](/en/docs/fields/number#step), for a number that isn’t meant to be stepped, like an ID copied from another system.
  * The new [`auto_increment`](/en/docs/fields/number#auto-increment) option numbers new entries automatically when they’re saved, like an `AUTO_INCREMENT` column in a relational database. The number can be used in the slug template, e.g. for invoices or podcast episodes.\[^404]
* [Object](/en/docs/fields/object)
  * Sveltia CMS offers two ways to have conditional fields in a collection:\[^30]
    * The Object widget supports [variable types](/en/docs/fields/object#variable-type) (the `types` and `typeKey` options) just like the List widget.\[^226]
    * An optional Object field (`required: false`) can be manually added or removed with a checkbox.\[^88] If unadded or removed, the required subfields won’t trigger validation errors,\[^16] and the field will be saved as `null`.
* [Relation](/en/docs/fields/relation)
  * Field options are displayed with no additional API requests.\[^14] The confusing `options_length` option, which defaults to 20, is therefore ignored.\[^76]
  * The widget reliably displays the selected option in the summary and all available options in the dropdown list.\[^259]
  * `slug` can be used for `value_field` to show all available options instead of just one in some situations.\[^91]
  * Template strings with a wildcard like `{{cities.*.name}}` can also be used for `value_field`.\[^94]
  * `display_fields` is displayed in the Preview Pane instead of `value_field`.
  * The redundant `search_fields` option is optional in Sveltia CMS, as it defaults to `display_fields`, `value_field` or the collection’s `identifier_field`, which is `title` by default.
  * The `value_field` option is also optional in Sveltia CMS, as it defaults to `{{slug}}` (entry slugs).
  * A new item created in a referenced collection is immediately available in the options.\[^138]
  * A related entry can be [created on the fly](/en/docs/fields/relation#creating-related-entries) from the Relation field itself, without leaving the entry being edited. The new entry is selected right away and saved along with the entry in the same commit.\[^266]
  * A referenced DateTime field value is displayed in the specified format.\[^221]
  * It’s possible to refer to a List field with the `field` option, which produces a single subfield but does not output the subfield `name` in the data, using the `value_field: cities.*.name` syntax. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/discussions/400))
  * Supports the `filters` option to filter available options based on field values in the referenced collection.\[^308]
    * The implementation is compatible with Decap CMS.
    * Sveltia CMS supports the [`exclude`](/en/docs/fields/relation#filters) option to exclude options based on field values in the referenced collection.
    * Template strings like `{{slug}}` and `{{fields.title}}` can also be used in the filter values.
    * A filter on a field holding multiple values, such as a [Select](/en/docs/fields/select) field with `multiple: true` or a [List](/en/docs/fields/list) field without subfields, matches an entry when any of its values is included in the filter values. A template string referring to such a field in the current entry is expanded to all of its values.\[^377]
  * The new [`sort_by`](/en/docs/fields/relation#sort-by) option sorts the options by any field in the referenced collection, such as a date, in ascending or descending order. By default, the options are sorted alphabetically by label, or follow the manual order of a collection with the `reorder` option.
  * Reverse relations can be displayed in the Content Editor’s [Backlinks sidebar panel](/en/docs/ui/content-editor#sidebar).
  * [Cascading updates and deletions](/en/docs/fields/relation#cascading-updates): When a referenced entry is renamed, the Relation field values pointing at it are updated; when it’s deleted, the references are removed. The deletion is refused if that would leave a `required` field empty or a multi-select field below its `min`, so referential integrity is maintained without breaking any entry.\[^243]
  * Multi-value Relation fields can be populated with comma-separated [dynamic default values](/en/docs/ui/content-editor#dynamic-default-values).\[^336]
* [Select](/en/docs/fields/select)
  * It’s possible to select an option with value `0`.\[^56]
  * `label` is displayed in the Preview Pane instead of `value`.
  * Option values can be [booleans or `null`](/en/docs/fields/select#boolean-and-null-values) in addition to strings and numbers, e.g. “Yes”, “No” and “Not relevant” choices stored as `true`, `false` and `null`. Netlify/Decap CMS only accepts strings and numbers, and fails to load such a configuration.
* [String](/en/docs/fields/string)
  * When a YouTube video URL is entered in a String field, it appears as an embedded video in the Preview Pane. Check your site’s [CSP](/en/docs/security#setting-up-content-security-policy) if the preview doesn’t work.
  * When a regular URL is entered in a String field, it appears as a link that can be opened in a new browser tab.
  * Supports the `type` option that accepts `url` or `email` as a value, which will validate the value as a URL or email.
  * Supports the `prefix` and `suffix` string options, which automatically prepend and/or append the developer-defined value to the user-input value, if it’s not empty.
* [Boolean](/en/docs/fields/boolean), [Number](/en/docs/fields/number) and [String](/en/docs/fields/string)
  * Supports the `before_input` and `after_input` string options, which allow developers to display custom labels before and/or after the input UI.\[^28] Markdown is supported in the value.
    * Compatibility note: In Static CMS, these options are implemented as `prefix` and `suffix`, respectively, which have different meaning in Sveltia CMS.
* [File](/en/docs/fields/file) and [Image](/en/docs/fields/image)
  * Provides a reimagined all-in-one asset selection dialog for File and Image fields.\[^234]
    * Field, entry, file, [collection](/en/docs/media/internal#collection-level-configuration) and global assets are listed on separate tabs for easy selection.\[^19]
    * A new asset can be uploaded by dragging & dropping it into the dialog.\[^20]
    * A URL can also be entered in the dialog.
    * Integration with Pexels, Pixabay and Unsplash makes it easy to select and insert a free stock photo.\[^8] More stock photo providers will be added in the future.
  * Users can also simply drag and drop a file onto a File/Image field to attach it without having to open the Select File dialog.
  * Users can paste an image from the clipboard directly into a File or Image field by clicking the Paste button.
  * Supports the boolean `multiple` option, which can be set to `true` to allow multiple file uploads.\[^239]
    * When enabled, users can select and upload multiple files at once in the Select File dialog, as well as drag and drop multiple files onto the field. The field value will be an array of strings instead of a single string.
    * The `min` and `max` options are also available to limit the number of files that can be uploaded. Both accept positive integers. If `min` is not specified, it defaults to `0`. If `max` is not specified, it defaults to `Infinity`.
  * The new `accept` option allows files to be filtered by a comma-separated list of unique file type specifiers, in the same way as the HTML [`accept` attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/accept) for `<input type="file">`.\[^216]
    * By default, the Image widget only accepts an AVIF, GIF, JPEG, PNG, WebP or SVG image. BMP, HEIC, JPEG XL, PSD, TIFF and other less common or non-standard files are excluded,\[^217] except that HEIC photos are accepted when [HEIC conversion](/en/docs/media#heic-photos) is enabled.
    * The File widget has no default restriction.
  * If the collection’s `public_folder` contains `{{slug}}` and a slug field (e.g. `title`) of a new entry has been edited after uploading an asset, the updated slug will be used in the saved asset path.\[^140] Other dynamic template tags such as `{{filename}}` will also be populated as expected.\[^141]
  * The CMS prevents the same file from being uploaded twice. It compares the hashes and selects an existing asset instead.
  * Large images automatically fit in the Preview Pane instead of being displayed at their original size, which can easily exceed the width of the pane.
  * Image thumbnails are displayed in the Edit Pane as expected.\[^333]\[^337]
  * Unsaved files can be renamed.
  * The File field supports the `select_folder` option, compatible with Static CMS, to select a folder instead of a file. The Select Folder dialog works like a file manager: a click selects a folder, a double click opens it, and the arrow keys move between folders. With the `multiple` option, several folders can be selected at once.
* [List](/en/docs/fields/list) and [Object](/en/docs/fields/object)
  * The `summary` is displayed correctly when it refers to a Relation field\[^36] or a simple List field.
  * The `summary` template tags support [transformations](/en/docs/string-transformations), e.g. `{{fields.date | date('YYYY-MM-DD')}}`.
  * The `collapsed` option accepts the value `auto` to automatically collapse the widget if any of its subfields are filled out. The same applies to the `minimize_collapsed` option for the List widget.
  * The new `thumbnail` option allows developers to specify an Image or File subfield name, including a nested one like `mobile.src`, for the thumbnail of a collapsed list item or object. Thumbnails are displayed alongside the `summary`.
  * A variable type can have a `description`, displayed below its label in the Add button’s dropdown menu, and a `hint`, displayed above its subfields like a field’s `hint`.\[^417]
  * A removed list item, optional object or variable type object is replaced with a notice and a Restore button, so it can be brought back with all its values if it was removed by mistake.\[^418]
* [Markdown](/en/docs/fields/markdown), [String](/en/docs/fields/string) and [Text](/en/docs/fields/text)
  * Emoji autocomplete is enabled by default, allowing users to type `:` followed by a few letters to search for an emoji.
  * A required field containing only spaces or line breaks will result in a validation error, as if no characters were entered.
* [Relation](/en/docs/fields/relation) and [Select](/en/docs/fields/select)
  * Selected items can be reordered.\[^394]
  * If a dropdown list has options with long wrapping labels, they won’t overlap with the next option.\[^83]
  * When there are 5 or fewer options, the UI automatically switches from a dropdown list to radio buttons (single-select) or checkboxes (multi-select) for faster data entry.\[^61] This number can be changed with the `dropdown_threshold` option for the `relation` and `select` widgets.
* [String](/en/docs/fields/string) and [Text](/en/docs/fields/text)
  * Supports the `minlength` and `maxlength` options, which allow developers to specify the minimum and maximum number of characters required for input without having to write a custom regular expression with the `pattern` option. A character counter is available when one of the options is given, and a user-friendly validation error is displayed if the condition is not met.

The following new widgets are available in Sveltia CMS:

* [Compute](/en/docs/fields/compute)
  * The experimental `compute` widget allows to reference the value of other fields in the same collection, similar to the `summary` property for the List and Object widgets.\[^104] Use the `value` property to define the value template, e.g. `posts-{{fields.slug}}`. ([Example](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/111))
  * The `value` property also supports a value of `{{index}}`, which can hold the index of a list item. ([Example](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/172))
  * The `value` property also supports the `{{uuid}}`, `{{uuid_short}}` and `{{uuid_shorter}}` tags, which generate a random UUID that is kept once the entry is saved. ([Example](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/122))
* [KeyValue](/en/docs/fields/keyvalue) (Dictionary)
  * The new `keyvalue` widget allows users to add arbitrary key-value string pairs to a field.\[^123]
  * While the implementation is compatible with [Static CMS](https://staticjscms.netlify.app/docs/widget-keyvalue), we provide a more intuitive UI. Users can press Enter to move focus or add a new row while editing, and the preview is displayed in a clean table.
  * The `root` option is also available for a top-level key-value field, just like the List widget.
  * Key-value pairs can be reordered, and the new order is saved. ([Discussion](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/issues/1020))
  * The `label_singular` option is available for the Add button, just like the List widget.
  * An empty field shows a blank row to type in, just like a simple List field.
* [RichText](/en/docs/fields/richtext)
  * The `richtext` widget is an alias of `markdown` that also supports HTML output. Set the `format` option to `html` to save the content as HTML instead of Markdown.\[^392] The option can also be set globally with `field_defaults`.
  * With the `html` format, the new [`align` button](/en/docs/fields/richtext#buttons) allows users to align paragraphs, headings, block quotes and list items to the left, center or right, or justify them. Add `align` to the `buttons` option to enable it.\[^406]
  * With the `html` format, the link editor offers an option to open a link in a new tab, which adds `target="_blank"` to the link.\[^407]
* [UUID](/en/docs/fields/uuid)
  * In addition to [generating UUIDs for entry slugs](/en/docs/collections/entries/slugs#slug-template-tags), Sveltia CMS supports the proposed `uuid` widget with the following properties:\[^12]
    * `prefix`: A string to be prepended to the value. Default: an empty string.
    * `use_b32_encoding`: Whether to encode the value with Base32. Default: `false`.

### Better Asset Management

* A completely new, full-fledged [Asset Library](/en/docs/ui/asset-library), built separately from the image selection dialog, makes it easy to manage all files, including images, videos and documents.\[^96]
  * Navigate between the global media folder and [collection media folders](/en/docs/media/internal#collection-level-configuration).\[^6]
  * Browse the [subfolders](/en/docs/ui/asset-library#subfolders) of a media folder, with a breadcrumb leading back to the parent folders, and create, rename and delete folders — a rename moves every asset in the folder and updates the entries referencing them, and a deletion removes the references in the same commit.\[^240] The Select File dialog lists and creates subfolders as well, and an uploaded file is saved to the folder being browsed. Netlify/Decap CMS lists every file in one flat view, and while its config can point a field at a subfolder, users can’t organize files into folders themselves. The same folder browsing works on [Amazon S3, the S3-compatible providers and Azure Blob Storage](/en/docs/ui/asset-library#folders-on-external-locations), which store files at paths.
  * Preview image, audio, video, text and PDF files. Check your site’s [CSP](/en/docs/security#setting-up-content-security-policy) if the preview doesn’t work.
  * Copy the public URL,\[^74] file path, text data or image data of a selected asset to clipboard. The file path starts with `/` as expected.\[^48]
  * Edit plain text assets, including SVG images.
  * Rename existing assets. If the asset is used in any entries, the File/Image fields will be automatically updated with a new file path.
  * Replace existing assets.
  * Download one or more selected assets at once.
  * Delete one or more selected assets at once. If an asset is used in any entries, the File/Image fields and Markdown images referencing it are [removed in the same commit](/en/docs/ui/asset-library#asset-management), and the deletion is refused if that would leave a required field empty or a multi-file field below its `min`, so a required image can’t be deleted by accident.
  * Upload multiple assets at once, including files in nested folders, by browsing or dragging and dropping them into the library.
  * Sort or filter assets by name or file type.
  * View asset details, including size, dimensions, commit author/date and a list of entries that use the selected asset.
  * View some Exif metadata if available, including the creation date and GPS coordinates displayed on a map.
  * Manage files stored on [external media storage providers](/en/docs/ui/asset-library#external-locations) such as Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Azure Blob Storage and Uploadcare from the same library. Users can browse, search, sort and filter the files, and upload, rename, replace, download or delete them where the service’s API allows, without switching to the provider’s dashboard. In Netlify/Decap CMS, external providers are only available through the image selection dialog.
  * The [Linked Files](/en/docs/ui/asset-library#linked-files) location gathers every file that a File/Image field links to by URL, wherever it’s hosted, so users can preview it and see which entries use it.
* Enhancements to media storage:
  * Supports multiple media storage providers with the [new `media_libraries` option](/en/docs/media#configuration).\[^195]
  * [Additional features](/en/docs/media#additional-features) are available for both internal and external media storage providers, except for Cloudinary:
    * A [built-in image optimizer](/en/docs/media#image-optimization): With a few lines of configuration, images selected by users for upload are automatically converted to WebP format for reduced size,\[^199] and it’s also possible to specify a maximum width and/or height.\[^200] [HEIC photos](/en/docs/media#heic-photos) from iPhones and Android phones, which browsers other than Safari can’t display, are converted too. SVG images can also be optimized.
    * [File size limits](/en/docs/media#file-size-limits) can be set for all media storage providers to prevent users from uploading excessively large files. In Netlify/Decap CMS, this option is only available at field level for the internal media storage provider, and it doesn’t apply to direct uploads to the Asset Library.
    * [Filename slugification](/en/docs/media#slugification-of-filenames) can be configured for all media storage providers.
  * [Internal media storage provider](/en/docs/media/internal)
    * With [asset collections](/en/docs/media/internal#asset-collections), users can organize assets into multiple folders that are displayed in the Asset Library and the Select File dialog. These folders can be used across multiple collections. This feature is useful for managing assets by type, topic, or project.
    * It supports multiple file selection.\[^239] This can be enabled by setting the new `multiple` File/Image widget option to `true`. For compatibility with other media storage providers, the `media_library.config.multiple` option is also supported.
    * Unlike Netlify/Decap CMS, files are uploaded with their original names. Sanitization is still applied to avoid issues with special characters, but uppercase letters and spaces are not converted to lowercase letters and hyphens.\[^97] If you want to slugify filenames, use the [`slugify_filename` media storage option](/en/docs/media#slugification-of-filenames). You can also rename uploaded files automatically with the [`filename_template` option](/en/docs/media#renaming-uploaded-files), using template tags like `{{slug}}` and `{{uuid_short}}`.\[^385]
  * [Cloudinary](/en/docs/media/cloudinary)
    * Field-specific media storage configuration works as expected.\[^297]
    * When the `multiple` option is enabled, the output is always an array of strings, regardless of whether a single file is selected.\[^299]
    * The `script-src` CSP directive is not required for the widget to work, as we implemented the Cloudinary media storage without using their hosted widget script.
    * Image previews work as expected when the `output_filename_only` option is `true`.\[^327]
  * [Uploadcare](/en/docs/media/uploadcare)
    * An API-based integration allows users to select existing files from their Uploadcare account.\[^247]
    * Supports [signed uploads](https://uploadcare.com/docs/security/secure-uploads/) to prevent unauthorized uploads. Files are uploaded with a signature computed using your secret key.
    * No error is raised for file collections if the `media_folder` option is not defined.\[^295]
  * Other integrations
    * Integrates [stock photo providers](/en/docs/integrations/stock-photos), including Pexels, Pixabay and Unsplash.\[^8] Lorem Picsum can be used as a free placeholder image provider without having to obtain an API key.
    * Integrates [Amazon S3](/en/docs/media/amazon-s3) and S3-compatible storage providers, including [Cloudflare R2](/en/docs/media/cloudflare-r2) and [DigitalOcean Spaces](/en/docs/media/digitalocean-spaces).\[^315]
    * More integration options will be added in the future.
* Assets stored in an [entry-relative media folder](/en/docs/media/internal#using-entry-relative-folders) are handled as part of the entry.
  * These assets are displayed in the Asset Library.\[^142]
  * They are automatically deleted when the associated entry is deleted because these are not available for other entries.\[^22] When you’re [working with a local repository](/en/docs/workflows/local), the empty enclosing folder is also deleted.
  * They are copied along with the entry when it’s duplicated, so a duplicated Hugo [page bundle](https://gohugo.io/content-management/page-bundles/) doesn’t end up referencing images that only exist in the original’s folder. Netlify/Decap CMS simply copies the field values, leaving the new entry with broken image references.
* Assets stored in the subfolders of `media_folder` are scanned recursively and displayed in the Asset Library.\[^249]
* The global `media_folder` can be an empty string (or `.` or `/`) if you want to store assets in the root folder.
* PDF documents are displayed with a thumbnail image in both the Asset Library and the Select File dialog, making it easier to find the file they’re looking for.\[^38]
* Hidden files (dot files) don’t appear in the Asset Library.\[^47]
* Users can add assets using the Quick Add button in the upper right corner of the application.
* Rather than automatically renaming a file with an existing name when it is uploaded, the CMS prompts the user to either replace the existing file or rename the new one.
* Warnings are issued before corrupt or mislabeled files, such as a HEIC image saved with a `.jpg` extension, are uploaded.

### Better Workflows

* [Local Workflow](/en/docs/workflows/local) enhancements:
  * We have eliminated the need for additional configuration and a proxy server, resulting in a streamlined workflow and improved performance.\[^26]
  * It also avoids a number of issues, including potential security risks,\[^158]\[^282]\[^318]\[^340] a 30 MB file size limit,\[^51] an unknown error with `publish_mode`,\[^75] and an unused `logo_url`.\[^49]
  * When you delete an entry or an asset file, the empty folder that contains it is also deleted, so it doesn’t have to be deleted manually.
  * The CMS can [commit your changes](/en/docs/workflows/local#git-commits) to the current branch of the local repository every time you save. Netlify/Decap CMS only offers this through an experimental, undocumented option of its proxy server.\[^402] Sveltia CMS commits only the files it saves, leaving your other work in progress alone, and tells you why when it can’t commit, such as when a merge is in progress.
* [Preview Workflow](/en/docs/workflows/preview) is available as a new `preview` publish mode. Each change is saved to a pull request, so it can be checked on a deploy preview, and published straight away, without the review stages of Editorial Workflow. Netlify/Decap CMS offers no way to save a change without publishing it short of the full Editorial Workflow.\[^261]
* [Editorial Workflow](/en/docs/workflows/editorial) enhancements:
  * Editorial Workflow works with the [Gitea/Forgejo backend](/en/docs/backends/gitea-forgejo) as well as GitHub and GitLab.\[^391]
  * Performance is much better than with Netlify/Decap CMS, as we use the GraphQL API wherever possible.\[^348]
  * Sveltia CMS does not use the GitHub `compare` API to avoid the 250-commit limit.\[^349]
  * Unpublished entries are listed at the top of each entry collection page, along with status indicators.\[^350]
  * The Editorial Workflow board and the unpublished entries keep up with pull requests opened, updated, merged or closed outside the CMS — by a colleague, a bot, or a merge on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or Forgejo — without a page reload, and the board has a Refresh button for when you can’t wait. Netlify/Decap CMS reads the pull requests once, when the Workflow page or a collection is first opened, and offers no way to read them again, so a change made elsewhere only shows up after the page is reloaded. See [Editorial Workflow Page](/en/docs/workflows/editorial#editorial-workflow-page).
  * Draft entries are kept as [draft pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/create-pull-requests/changing-the-stage-of-a-pull-request) or [draft merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/drafts/), making it easier to identify them in the repository.
  * Entry deletions go through the Editorial Workflow instead of being committed directly, whether a user deletes a single entry in the Content Editor or several at once from the entry list, and Sveltia CMS doesn’t implement the confusing unpublishing process.\[^351]
  * The Publish button is only displayed when the entry has reached the last stage, Ready by default.
  * The `publish_mode` option also takes an [object form](/en/docs/workflows/editorial#options) with more options:
    * `stages` leaves out the In Review or Ready stage, so a team that doesn’t need a separate review step can mark a saved draft ready, or publish it once it’s in review. Netlify/Decap CMS always requires a draft to be moved to Ready before it can be published.\[^415]
    * `direct_publish` adds Save and Publish to the Save button, so a quick fix can go live in one go — straight to the configured branch, or by merging the entry’s pull request — while other changes still go through review. With Netlify/Decap CMS, publishing a change takes six clicks across saving, changing the status and confirming.\[^416]
    * `allow_incomplete_drafts: false` enforces required fields in drafts as well, for sites that prefer the Netlify/Decap CMS behavior.
  * The Publish button is hidden from users who can’t merge into the configured branch on GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo, such as a Developer on a branch that only Maintainers can merge into.\[^388]
  * Saving an entry offers to send it for review there and then, so a draft isn’t left sitting with no pull request because the status menu went unnoticed.\[^352]
  * Required fields aren’t enforced while an entry is in draft, so unfinished work can be saved without filling in every field or padding them with placeholder values. This can be turned off with the `allow_incomplete_drafts` option.\[^361]
  * Unpublished entries are included in search results and in the entry counts shown in the collection list, so a draft isn’t hidden just because it hasn’t been published yet.
  * Editorial Workflow works on a forked repository. Netlify/Decap CMS looks each pull request up with a `head=[OWNER]:[BRANCH]` filter, which GitHub resolves against the upstream network on a fork, so no unpublished entry is ever found. Sveltia CMS lists the pull requests once and matches them locally.\[^354]
  * An unpublished entry is reconstructed only from the pull request files that belong to the collection its branch names, so unrelated files committed alongside it — generated content, assets, or entries from another collection — can’t be mistaken for the entry. Netlify/Decap CMS filters the files by extension alone and then picks the first match, which loads the wrong file when anything else in the repository shares the extension.\[^355]
  * The current HEAD SHA of the source branch is included in publish requests for the GitLab editorial workflow, which may be required by a group or instance.\[^360]
  * The `publish_mode` option can be set per collection, so a review process can be required for some collections and skipped for others, such as a site settings collection, rather than switched on or off for the whole site.\[^375]
  * A workflow branch is named after the entry, not the editor, so two people working on the same entry share it. Sveltia CMS compares the branch with the draft when the entry is saved and asks before writing over a change someone else has made to the entry. Netlify/Decap CMS rebases the branch but doesn’t handle the conflict, so the second save overwrites the first with nothing said.\[^389]
  * A pull request is taken for an entry’s own only if it holds one of the entry’s files, not merely because it comes from the branch named after the entry. Netlify/Decap CMS goes by the branch name alone, so a pull request from that branch holding something else is shown, and published, as the entry.
  * Publishing an entry checks the pull request first: it has to go to the configured branch, still point at the commit the entry was loaded or saved at, and change nothing the CMS doesn’t account for, such as the site’s code or another entry. The merge is then pinned to that commit. Netlify/Decap CMS merges the pull request as it stands, so anything else pushed to the branch goes live along with the entry unseen; when GitHub can’t merge it, Decap CMS even copies its files onto the configured branch regardless. See [Checks Before Publishing](/en/docs/workflows/editorial#checks-before-publishing).
* [Open Authoring](/en/docs/workflows/open) enhancements:
  * Open Authoring works with the GitLab and [Gitea/Forgejo](/en/docs/backends/gitea-forgejo) backends as well as GitHub.\[^390]
  * Moving an entry back to Draft marks its pull request as a draft rather than closing it, so the review discussion, approvals and checks on it survive. Netlify/Decap CMS closes the pull request and reopens it later.
  * The contributor’s fork is found even when it isn’t at the name GitHub gives it by default — because they renamed it, because your repository was renamed after they forked it, or because they already had a repository of that name and GitHub added a suffix. Netlify/Decap CMS only looks for a fork at `[USER_NAME]/[REPOSITORY_NAME]`, so a fork anywhere else is missed and the contributor is asked to create one on every sign-in.\[^420]
  * On GitHub and GitLab, a workflow branch starts from the head of the configured repository rather than from the contributor’s fork, so a fork that has fallen behind or gained commits of its own doesn’t pass them on. Netlify/Decap CMS branches from the fork, where an out-of-date one leaks unrelated changes into the pull request.\[^353] Gitea and Forgejo can’t branch from a commit the fork doesn’t have, so the CMS brings the fork up to date on sign-in instead, with each service’s own API for it.
  * Problems while setting Open Authoring up are reported with something to act on, rather than a generic failure: a repository invitation that hasn’t been accepted yet, a sign-in that doesn’t cover private repositories, and a repository that doesn’t allow forks are each named specifically.
  * Whether the signed-in user is a maintainer is determined from the repository’s own permissions, which any access level can read, rather than from the collaborator endpoint that needs administrator access to answer.
  * Uploads to the Media Library are disabled for contributors. Netlify/Decap CMS uploads files to a fork without creating a pull request.
  * A banner appears with the name of a fork the contributor’s changes are being saved to, with a link to it, so it’s clear where their work is going.
  * Saving an entry offers to send it for review there and then, which is what opens the pull request. Otherwise a contributor’s first save leaves their work sitting in their fork with nothing for a maintainer to see.\[^352]
  * The entry list and the entry editor toolbar are updated immediately after saving a draft.
* [Deploy Previews](/en/docs/workflows/deploy-previews) enhancements:
  * The build state is reported in [Simple Workflow](/en/docs/workflows/simple) too, so it’s clear when an edit is actually live. Netlify/Decap CMS never asks the backend and always presents the link as ready, whether the page has been rebuilt or not.
  * Deployments and environments are read as well as commit statuses. Netlify/Decap CMS reads commit statuses alone, missing GitHub Pages and GitLab Review Apps.
  * A deployment’s environment URL is preferred over a commit status target URL, which often points to a build log rather than the site. Netlify/Decap CMS only looks at the status, so a CI/CD service that reports the preview as a GitHub deployment gets no link.\[^395]
  * Check runs are read too, including the URLs a provider publishes in the run’s output — where [Cloudflare Pages](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/git-integration/github-integration/) writes its preview address while linking the check at its own dashboard. A run’s own link is followed only when its name says preview, as [AWS Amplify](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/pr-previews.html)’s does; every other run still reports its build state.\[^356]
  * A build that was canceled or skipped is ignored, even when the provider reports it as successful — the monorepo case, where a site the commit didn’t touch still reports a result. Netlify/Decap CMS takes the first matching status, so it links to the canceled build’s log.\[^357]
  * A failed build is reported as such, and while a preview is building the control says so and waits instead of offering the live site. Netlify/Decap CMS shows a Check for Preview button that never resolves, with no sign of whether the build failed or is merely slow.\[^358]
  * A running build is re-checked every five seconds for ten minutes, and when the CMS gives up it says so and offers a manual re-check. Netlify/Decap CMS polls at the same rate for about two minutes — often too short for a slow build — and gives no sign that it has stopped.\[^359]
  * The [Gitea/Forgejo](/en/docs/backends/gitea-forgejo) backend supports deploy previews too, read from commit statuses. Netlify/Decap CMS’s Gitea backend doesn’t implement them, so its entries never link to a preview.
  * On GitHub, all three sources are fetched in one request, so watching a build costs a single call per check. They’re split apart only for a repository that can’t answer for one of them, which is discovered once rather than assumed. GitLab has no bulk equivalent, so there it costs one shared call plus one per commit watched, and on Gitea/Forgejo one per commit watched.
  * When `site_url` isn’t configured, the production deployment’s own URL is used instead, so preview links still work.
  * Where the CMS is served from the site it edits, the page itself is requested to confirm it’s live, so a finished build whose CDN hasn’t caught up is reported as still building rather than handed over as a link that 404s. A cross-origin page is skipped, since the browser couldn’t read the answer.
  * The `preview_context` option matches a name exactly, as in Netlify/Decap CMS, then falls back to a partial, case-insensitive match instead of silently finding nothing.
  * The `{{locale}}` template tag in the [`preview_path`](/en/docs/collections/entries/previews#preview-paths) collection option gives each language its own preview link, offered from the locale pane’s options menu in the Content Editor — deploy previews included, so every translation of an unpublished entry links to its own page on the build. Netlify/Decap CMS formats one URL per entry with no locale involved, leaving only the default language reachable.\[^63]
    * The new [`omit_default_locale_from_preview_path` option](/en/docs/i18n/slugs#preview-paths) excludes the default locale from preview paths, for sites that don’t include it in their URLs.
  * A `preview_path` using date tags is validated against the collection’s fields, so a template that could never be filled in is reported as a configuration warning instead of silently producing no link.
  * The Editorial Workflow board shows a preview link and a build badge on each card, so a failed build is visible without opening the entry.

### Better Customization

* It’s possible to display a custom application title on the login page and in the browser tab by setting the [`app_title`](/en/docs/customization#custom-application-title) property.
* A custom logo defined with the `logo_url` property is displayed on the global application header and the browser tab (favicon).\[^134] A smaller logo is also correctly positioned on the authentication page.\[^135]
* Developers can specify the URL to redirect users after logging out with the `logout_redirect_url` global option.\[^283]
* Enhancements to [custom editor components](/en/docs/api/editor-components):
  * `CMS.registerEditorComponent()` accepts a component definition with the `icon` property. Developers can specify a Material Symbols icon name just like [custom collection icons](/en/docs/collections#icons).
  * The `fromBlock` function can be omitted if the `pattern` regex contains [named capturing groups](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Named_capturing_group) for the values.
  * Inline components are supported.\[^267]
  * Field validation works as expected.\[^279]
  * No error is raised in the browser console saying `Sent invalid data to remark`\[^280] or `onValidate is not a function`.\[^281]
  * A link with kramdown inline attributes (e.g. `{:.class}`) is parsed correctly.\[^317]
  * Markdown is parsed and rendered correctly in the editor component preview.\[^330]
  * A File or Image field in a component can have its own `media_folder`. A relative folder is resolved against the entry being edited, so the file picker lists the files stored next to it, like in a Hugo page bundle. In Netlify/Decap CMS, the picker finds no files at all.\[^396]
  * Image, video and audio file paths are automatically replaced with blob URLs in the editor component preview if necessary, so that the files are displayed correctly. In Netlify/Decap CMS, you have to use the undocumented `getAsset` and `fields` parameters for the `toPreview` function to achieve this. Sveltia CMS supports these parameters as well, and [documents them](/en/docs/api/editor-components#displaying-assets), for other kinds of files and previews that need the URL.
  * The `toPreview` function can return a [DOM element](/en/docs/api/editor-components#using-a-framework-component-for-preview) in addition to a string or React element, so a preview can be rendered with a Svelte, Vue or other framework component.
  * The new [`CMS.renderRichText()`](/en/docs/api/rendering-markdown) method renders the value of a nested RichText field into a DOM element or React element preview with the same pipeline as the preview pane, so nested components, images and Markdown formatting all appear as they do in the parent field, without any parsing or sanitizing on the developer’s side. The value is always passed to `toPreview` as is, regardless of the order in which components are registered, so it can also be processed manually.
  * The new `mode` option accepts the value `dialog` to allow users to edit the component content in a dialog instead of the default block UI within the editor.
  * The `mode` option also accepts the value [`inline`](/en/docs/api/editor-components#status-select-inline-mode), which renders the control of the component’s only field, such as a select box or a date picker, right within the text.\[^267]
  * The new `trigger` option accepts the value `button`, which places the component directly on the toolbar rather than a menu item.
* Enhancements to [event hooks](/en/docs/api/events):
  * Missing `identifier_field` won’t cause an error when the `preSave` hook is triggered.\[^306]
* Enhancements to custom field types (widgets):
  * The API method has been renamed from `CMS.registerWidget()` to `CMS.registerFieldType()` for better clarity, while keeping the old name for backward compatibility.\[^314]
  * To prevent the app from crashing, registering built-in field type names is disallowed.
  * A control can hand files to the CMS with the documented [`addFile` prop](/en/docs/api/field-types#uploading-files), which replaces the undocumented `onPersistMedia` prop.\[^372] Compared to the Netlify/Decap CMS implementation:
    * It resolves to a URL that goes straight into the field value, and the CMS turns it into the public path on save. `onPersistMedia` returns an internal repository path in a Redux action, leaving each widget to guess the public path from it.
    * File naming, deduplication, `media_folder` resolution and `media_library` options work exactly as for a built-in File/Image field, including template tags like `{{slug}}`, which Netlify/Decap CMS can’t apply because it fixes the path as soon as the file is added.
    * The files are included in the same commit as the entry, so it works with the Editorial Workflow and Open Authoring.
  * A control can let the user pick a file with the documented [`pickFile` prop](/en/docs/api/field-types#picking-files), which opens the same dialog as a built-in File/Image field and replaces the undocumented `onOpenMediaLibrary`, `mediaPaths`, `onClearMediaControl` and `onRemoveInsertedMedia` props.\[^373] Compared to the Netlify/Decap CMS implementation:
    * It returns a Promise that resolves with the picked file once the dialog is closed, or `null` if it’s dismissed. In Netlify/Decap CMS, the widget has to generate its own control ID, open the library with it, watch the `mediaPaths` Redux state in `componentDidUpdate` for a path keyed by that ID, and then reset the state itself, with nothing to tell it that the dialog was canceled.
    * It provides the contents of the picked file as a `Blob`, so a control can derive a thumbnail or read metadata from an existing file. Netlify/Decap CMS only delivers the path.
    * It resolves with exactly what a built-in File/Image field would store, including a temporary URL for a file uploaded through the dialog, which is turned into the public path on save.
  * The undocumented definition object format of `CMS.registerWidget()`, i.e. `{ name, controlComponent, previewComponent, schema }`, is [supported and documented](/en/docs/api/field-types#registering-a-custom-field-type),\[^414] with an additional `summaryComponent` option that draws a collapsed List field item when the List field has a single subfield of the type. In Netlify/Decap CMS, a collapsed item can only show the text made from the `summary` option, so a field type storing a file path or an ID shows the raw value.
* Async functions can be used for [custom parsers/formatters](/en/docs/api/file-formats).\[^149]
* Developers can add [custom pages](/en/docs/api/custom-pages) to the global toolbar with the new `CMS.registerCustomPage()` method. A page can render a React component, embed another web page, such as an analytics dashboard, or link to an external site.\[^413]
* The application renders within the dimensions of a [custom mount element](/en/docs/customization#custom-mount-element), if exists.\[^109]
* Sveltia CMS exposes `React.Fragment` globally as `rf`, allowing developers to use it in custom editor components and field types without having to import React explicitly.
* Sveltia CMS exposes its bundled React as `CMS.React`, so [custom preview templates, editor components and field types](/en/docs/api#using-hooks) can use hooks, without adding another global.\[^382]
* Sveltia CMS exposes the [HTM](/en/docs/api#using-htm) tagged template globally as `html`, so developers can write custom preview templates, editor components and field types in JSX-like markup without a build step, instead of nesting `h()` calls. String `style` attributes and HTML attribute names like `class` and `for` work as in HTML.
* Sveltia CMS offers the `CMS.renderRichText()` method and exposes `marked` and `DOMPurify` for easier [Markdown rendering](/en/docs/api/rendering-markdown) in custom previews and field types.

### Better Localization

* Users can select the application UI locale. The `locale` configuration option is ignored in Sveltia CMS.
  * The initial locale is automatically selected based on the preferred language set with the browser.\[^132]
  * The CMS will prompt the user to switch to their language when it becomes available.
  * Users can change the locale in the application settings.
* Manual locale registration with `CMS.registerLocale()` is no longer required as the CMS automatically downloads a locale file from the CDN when a locale is selected.
* We use our own [Sveltia I18n](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-i18n) library for localization. Thanks to the [Unicode MessageFormat 2](https://messageformat.unicode.org/) (MF2) syntax, it provides better support for complex pluralization, allowing for more natural translations in different languages.
* The application layout automatically adjusts to support right-to-left (RTL) languages such as Arabic, Hebrew and Persian.\[^245]
* The List widget’s `label` and `label_singular` are not converted to lowercase, which is especially problematic in German, where all nouns are capitalized.\[^98]
* Long menu item labels, especially in non-English locales, don’t overflow the dropdown container.\[^117]\[^265]
* We maintain a [list of available locales](/en/docs/ui#localization) in our documentation. In contrast, Netlify/Decap CMS doesn’t provide a list even though manual registration is required.
* We provide a [localization guide](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms/blob/main/src/lib/locales/README.md) for translators to help them contribute translations for new locales or update existing ones.

### Better Documentation

* We provide well-structured and comprehensive documentation with detailed guides and examples to help you configure and use Sveltia CMS effectively. Compare some documents:
  * String Transformations: [Sveltia CMS](/en/docs/string-transformations) vs. [Netlify/Decap CMS](https://decapcms.org/docs/summary-strings/)
  * Custom File Formats: [Sveltia CMS](/en/docs/api/file-formats) vs. [Netlify/Decap CMS](https://decapcms.org/docs/custom-formatters/)
* We constantly update our documentation to reflect the latest features and improvements, ensuring that you have access to the most accurate and up-to-date information. In contrast, Decap CMS documentation is often outdated, incomplete and lacks important details. It makes no mention of the deprecation of Git Gateway, and even some new options remain undocumented. The Decap CMS team has never learned from Netlify CMS, which left various options and features undocumented.
* The site navigation is clearer and more organized, with separate pages created for each field type and the JavaScript API distinguished.\[^323]
* Our documentation supports dark mode for better readability in low-light environments.
* Code snippets can be copied to the clipboard with a single click, making it easier to use them in your own projects.
* Configuration examples are provided in YAML, TOML, JSON and JavaScript formats, allowing you to choose the format that best suits your needs.
* [API](/en/docs/api) examples involving React components are provided in [HTM](/en/docs/api#using-htm), JSX and `h()` syntax, allowing you to choose the one that best fits your project.
* We provide clear [migration instructions from Netlify CMS](/en/docs/migration/netlify-decap-cms), including step-by-step guides and best practices to ensure a smooth transition.
* Our [compatibility information](/en/docs/migration/netlify-decap-cms#compatibility) to help you avoid unsupported options and configurations that might cause errors. By contrast, the Netlify/Decap CMS documentation does not mention anything about the deprecation of camel case options, the removal of the Date widget and the replacement of Moment.js. Furthermore, the [Decap blog](https://decapcms.org/blog/decap-3/) claims that Decap CMS 3.0 is ”fully backward compatible” even though it removed the Date widget.
* Our [framework guides](/en/docs/frameworks) include starter templates, real-world examples and features for popular frameworks like Astro, Eleventy, and Hugo, making it easier to integrate Sveltia CMS into your projects.
* We don’t claim that the CMS can be used “with just a few clicks,” as this would be misleading for those setting it up for the first time.\[^328]
* We have listed some [common use cases](/en/docs/intro#use-cases) of the CMS in the introduction.\[^320] In addition, we have a dedicated [Showcase](/en/showcase) page featuring real-world examples of websites using Sveltia CMS.
  * The showcase is an important complement to the documentation as it provides practical examples of how the CMS can be used in different scenarios, helping users understand its capabilities and potential applications.
* Our [Content Modeling Guide](/en/docs/content-modeling#nonprofit-organization-site) provides detailed examples of how to model content for common examples, including collections, fields, and relationships between them, with complete configuration examples in YAML, TOML, JSON and JavaScript formats.\[^399]
* We document how the [collection-level `media_folder` option](/en/docs/media/internal#collection-level-configuration) works with a relative or absolute path.\[^321]
* We document the [`CmsConfig` type](/en/docs/api/initialization#typing-the-configuration-object) available on the global `CMS` object, which provides type definitions for the configuration object in TypeScript. It’s undocumented in Netlify/Decap CMS.
* The Collapsible Note custom editor component example works as expected.\[^322]
* We provide an official Agent Skill and `llms.txt` to help you [use AI agents](/en/docs/working-with-ai) like GitHub Copilot, Claude and ChatGPT more effectively when writing Sveltia CMS configuration files.
* The [entry summary documentation](/en/docs/collections/entries/listings#summaries) mentions that date-related template tags are not supported.\[^332]
* The [Gitea/Forgejo PKCE authorization](/en/docs/backends/gitea-forgejo#pkce-authorization) instructions include unchecking the **Confidential** option as a separate step, so you won’t miss it and get an `invalid empty client secret` error.\[^381]

## Ready to Migrate?

If you have scrolled this far, you must be interested in trying out Sveltia CMS! Check out the [migration guide](/en/docs/migration/netlify-decap-cms) to get started. Enjoy a significantly improved content management experience! 🚀
